enhancement.detailedExplanation:
ARTICLE 361A (Protection of publication of proceedings of Parliament and State Legislatures) is an essential structural provision in Part XIX: Miscellaneous of the Constitution of India.

### Operational Mechanics & Judicial Standards
In practice, ARTICLE 361A functions as a direct constitutional parameter binding executive and legislative action. The Supreme Court of India has consistently held that powers exercised under this provision are not unfettered; they must comply with the overarching constitutional discipline of the Rule of Law, Article 14 non-arbitrariness, and the basic features of the Constitution. Aggrieved parties may invoke the writ jurisdiction of the High Courts under Article 226 or the Supreme Court under Article 32 to challenge actions that transgress the constitutional boundaries of this article.

On judicial review, the High Court upholds the measure, confirming that the exercise of power conforms to Part XIX: Miscellaneous and constitutional safeguards.

Factual scenario (Ultra Vires Action): An authority bypasses the mandatory statutory prerequisites under ARTICLE 361A, acting arbitrarily or in excess of constitutional competence. The Supreme Court intervenes, holding that constitutional limitations cannot be sacrificed for administrative expediency, and quashes the impugned action.
distinctions: ARTICLE 361A vs General Administrative Power: Powers exercised under ARTICLE 361A derive directly from the Constitution and enjoy supremacy over ordinary statutes and subordinate rules.

ARTICLE 361A vs Fundamental Rights in Part III: Any measure enacted or executed under ARTICLE 361A remains subordinate to the Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 19, and 21 unless expressly protected by a saving clause.

Conclusion: The impugned order is ultra vires ARTICLE 361A and void for manifest arbitrariness under Article 14.
